description: Cross-page, cross-platform behavior patterns (.agents/patterns/README.md). Checked by tools/pattern_guard.py. canonical: files and symbols that own the behavior per platform; guards: regexes that must not match outside 'allow' (or listed 'debt') globs, ignoring comment lines.

patterns.title: Artwork background
patterns.summary: One decorative dimmed carousel behind the shell and splits, static focused song covers, reduced-motion still art and Data Saver no-art. Catalogue and cover failures recover with paced retries; known publication changes reset the pool, render/failure state and bounded ephemeral image cache even for identical URLs.

patterns.title: Scroll edge: content under pinned chrome
patterns.summary: Content is clear at any pinned edge (page/sheet header, pinned section title, bottom chrome) and ramps opaque over 40 units linear (top edges and every board footer with or without a player row, web Page useScrollMask; Apple and Android boards 40 since #329); accessibility settings give a hard cut, never content behind chrome; pinned titles are never dimmed; one mechanism per edge kind per platform.

guards.message: Scroll-content masks belong to the canonical edge-fade components (scroll-edge R1).
System scroll-edge effects are configured only by TopEdgeScrim and the modal shell (scroll-edge R1, R6).
A board's pinned footer and pager go through boardBottomChrome, so they read after the rows (scroll-edge R10).
Alpha masks for scroll edges belong to ui/common/ScrollEdgeFade.kt drawScrollEdgeRamp (scroll-edge R1).
Composition masks for scroll edges belong to TopEdgeFade/BoardFooterFade (scroll-edge R1).

patterns.title: Scroll indicators: system bars on every page
patterns.summary: Every page and sheet keeps the platform's own scroll indicators (Apple SwiftUI .automatic: shown while scrolling, macOS follows System Settings' Show scroll bars); no in-app scroll-bar setting (HIG Settings: don't duplicate global scrolling options; #356 agent decision); only paged carousels, the feedback attachment strip and the Paths chart hide theirs, with .hidden so macOS 'Always' still wins.

guards.message: Pages keep the system scroll indicators; only paged carousels, the attachment strip and the Paths chart hide theirs (scroll-indicators R1, R3).

patterns.title: Section-jump landing
patterns.summary: Quick Links and Songs section-index jumps land ordinary targets' titles (not their headers' padding) 32 units below chrome, keep the target current through arrival, and land pinned Songs titles at their pin line with the first row clear and never leave a large title resting part-way collapsed; a section index fits the height it is given, condensing its labels rather than growing the page, opens in its final layout without the region around it resizing, and its labels follow the text size within that fit; the index is one adjustable control assistive technologies can name and step.

guards.message: List landing correction belongs to SongsScrollChrome and the shared Quick Links path (section-jump-landing R1).
Lazy-list landing offsets belong to the shared Quick Links implementation (section-jump-landing R1).
Windows Songs jump pinning belongs to SongSectionHeader (section-jump-landing R1).

patterns.title: Section headers
patterns.summary: Section titles are white Title Case level-two headings above material cards; pinned Songs titles remain opaque and push one-for-one without overlap, the list end lets the last push finish, Songs titles its sections in every sort, A–Z included, and side-by-side card headers share their row's height so titles and cards start on one line.

guards.message: Pinned Songs header rendering belongs to SongsSectionBar (section-headers R4).
Pinned section headers belong to the canonical Songs list (section-headers R4).
The app says "View All", never "See All"; title-row links use SeeAllButton/ViewAllLinkText (section-headers R8, #321).

Full-line items in hinge-splitting grids use foldLaneItem so titles stay on their side of the fold (section-headers R10, #343, #584). Player Profile wraps its line-spanning rows in FoldLane (Overview fills one pane at a fold); the Shop header is a FoldLane; Player Bands moves its controls to their own pane at a hinge.
The Windows app says "View All", never "See All"; take the copy from ViewAllCta (ListLabel, ResultsLabel) (section-headers R8, view-all-cta R4; #321).
Windows pinned-header copies belong to SongsPage (section-headers R4, R6).
Apple 'open the full list' links and buttons read "View All", never "See All" (section-headers R8, view-all-cta R4; #321). Use SectionViewAllLink or PurpleActionLink.

patterns.title: Surface materials
patterns.summary: Use one native frosted material surface for content cards, rows and custom floating controls; reserve Liquid Glass and system materials for navigation and chrome; opaque fallbacks win for contrast and reduced transparency. Owner-approved #596 variant: the Apple profile's Duos, Trios and Quads band previews are one grouped card each (rows with hairlines, purple View All inside), unlike the web's per-band frosted cards. Android draws a long lazy list as one card from GlassCardSegment pieces (All Rivals, Rivalry, #603).

guards.message: Liquid Glass implementation (SwiftUI glassEffect or UIKit UIGlassEffect, including the #559 drawer search field backing) belongs only to GlassSurface (surface-materials R2).

Shipping Liquid Glass is only the drawer, the owner-approved iPhone Duo bottom search field (#358) and iPhone floating page tools (#632); other controls use festivalCardCapsule (surface-materials R1/R2).
Raw standard-material backgrounds belong in Design or an approved exception (surface-materials R3).

An opaque cardBackground plate is FestivalCardModifier's accessibility fallback, not a feature surface; draw cards, rows and custom floating controls with festivalCard / festivalCardCapsule (surface-materials R1, #319).
A gradient-stroked shape is shaded on the CPU each draw; draw the card rim with CardRim (a gradient view under a solid stroke mask) (surface-materials R9, #553).
The board pager draws on the rows' FSTCardSurfaceBrush / FSTCardStrokeBrush, never a pager-only plate (surface-materials R1, #319).

Each profile Bands group is one FSTRowsCardStyle card of BandCardView rows ending in the shared purple FSTViewAllButtonStyle CTA (owner-approved variant #596, surface-materials R7); do not bring back a frosted View All tile.

patterns.title: Page tools and navigation chrome
patterns.summary: Native shell navigation owns destinations; page tools use Apple's registry-drawn floating Liquid Glass buttons above every horizontal tab bar (iPhone, iPhone Duo inner portrait, compact iPad) with Notifications beside Profile in one header pill and leading titles (owner-approved, R28, #632; extended by agent decision #633: rail items on the Duo vertical bar, trailing bar items in the regular iPad sidebar shell, the Mac window toolbar with every toolbar item also a menu-bar command), Android floating toolbar at every window size (owner-approved, #576) or Windows title/page-header placement rather than a parallel command surface; every Apple page keeps its standard navigation title in every iPhone Duo pose, except song pages, which show their pinned song title only after the header scrolls away (owner-approved, #363); Android, Windows and Apple Rival pages name the rival and the section in the bar (Windows: the page header; Apple: R18's in-list InstrumentPageTitle with a subtitle line, pinned title over subtitle once it scrolls away): Rival Detail is the rival's name over "Rivals" or a single chart's "{icon} {Instrument} Rivals", Rivalry is the section over the rival's name (R23, #604); on the Android player page and Statistics only, Select/Switch/Deselect Profile is its own pill beside the floating toolbar in the same row (owner-approved, R24, #590); the drawer keeps its Deselect too. Apple system bar items (the iPhone Duo rail's board switchers, Choose Profile) keep their system metrics, and tests prove their 44 pt target by hit region, not by element frame (R27, agent decision #625). Windows page tools stay put while content scrolls: each page's header (title, Quick Links, Rank By, Select/Switch/Deselect Profile) sits above its ScrollViewer with content clipped under it, and Song Details' pinned bar carries Paths, Item Shop and Quick Links at one 40 epx height (R29, agent decision #639).

guards.message: Page tools float as individual glass buttons drawn by FloatingPageToolsBar wherever there is a horizontal tab bar, never a tab-bar accessory (owner-approved, page-tools-and-nav-chrome R28, #632, #633).

guards.regex: Button\("(Sort|Filter|Find Rival)…"\)|Toggle\("as (List|Grid)"|Menu\("(Rank By|Instrument|Band Size)"\)|"View Rival's Profile"
guards.message: The macOS and iPadOS menu bars lay out page tools only through the shared PageToolViewMenuItems / PageToolProfileMenuItems, so both menu bars and their tested mirror stay one implementation (page-tools-and-nav-chrome R28, #633).
Pages set their title mode with festivalTitleDisplayMode(_:), so iPhone titles stay leading beside the drawer or Back (owner-approved, page-tools-and-nav-chrome R28, #632).
The shell alone renders the floating toolbar, at every window size, plus the on-demand split's trailing pane for its own page (page-tools-and-nav-chrome R4, R6; split-panes R7).
The floating toolbar never hides on scroll, on any page (page-tools-and-nav-chrome R7, agent decision #577).
Global title-bar command content belongs to the main shell (page-tools-and-nav-chrome R5, R6).
Only the shell's profile item hides its toolbar glass, through profileItemBackground (page-tools-and-nav-chrome R8).
Pages keep the system navigation bar and its title in every pose; don't hide it (page-tools-and-nav-chrome R14, #341).
Shell chrome reads in hierarchy order; the order journeys cannot see a sort priority (page-tools-and-nav-chrome R17, #394).

A pushing page's search drawer goes through SongsSystemFilterField so SearchDrawerTransitionFill gives it the glass backing at every scroll position (#559) and draws its capsule during push and pop (page-tools-and-nav-chrome R19); the Profile sheet never pushes and keeps the system look.
Only FestivalScreen draws the top app bar, so every page title marquees through FestivalBarTitle (page-tools-and-nav-chrome R21, #597).

patterns.title: Modal shell
patterns.summary: All sheets, dialogs and alerts use the shared native shell for title, standard dismissal, Close behavior and presentation serialization; only the feedback form retains Cancel/Submit, and a filed form closes by itself before its single-Done result alert opens over Settings (#565); on Apple the feedback form takes dropped media and, on wide iPad/Duo, picks photos in a pane beside it; Paths on the unfolded or book-folded iPhone Duo, iPad and Mac opens over the whole window (full-screen cover; window-sized Mac sheet) through festivalModalPresentation, latched while open, with pull-down dismissal on iOS (owner-approved, #368); where the Apple Paths selector row is narrow (sheet window <= 768 pt, folded Duo) the Instrument and View menus show only their icon and Difficulty fills the row, like the web mobile PathsModal (owner-approved, #612); on Windows a body that can outgrow the window owns its ScrollViewer under a fixed title and command row, because ContentDialog's template scroller never scrolls vertically (agent decision, #420); on Android every sheet opens fully expanded with no half-height stop (agent decision, #586), and no sheet or dialog draws a line under the shared header (owner, #607); the Windows Paths compact selectors likewise show only the instrument and Image/Text icons when icon + name do not fit on one line (ComboBoxFaceTemplateSelector; owner-approved, #612); while the feedback form sends and files, its fields fade out to a centred white spinner with a title and subtitle (Uploading Media over a determinate bar, then Filing Issue/Request), the spinner staying across the cross-fade (owner-approved, #634; Apple, Android, Windows; without media it reads as filing from Submit); on Windows the Notifications bell opens the shared dialog docked to the window edge: a full-height trailing panel below the title bar like the web desktop drawer, or a full-width bottom sheet once navigation collapses to the hamburger menu (DialogChrome.WindowEdge, ModalEdgeLayout; owner-approved, #638, Windows Notifications only).

guards.message: Create WinUI dialogs through FestivalDialog (modal-shell R1).
Create Material bottom sheets through FestivalModalSheet (modal-shell R1).
Create Material alerts through FestivalAlertDialog (modal-shell R1).
Modal Close belongs to FestivalSheetCloseItem, not a hand-made toolbar control (modal-shell R4).
Keep surfaces off a separating hinge through core/nav HingeSide; adapt its result, don't add another side rule (modal-shell R8).
Centred dialogs take the window width less 16 dp margins, capped at 560 dp, never the platform dialog width (modal-shell R9).
Sheets open fully expanded with no half-height stop; never pass skipPartiallyExpanded other than true (modal-shell R13, #586).
ContentDialog's template scroller never scrolls vertically; give a tall body its own ScrollViewer instead of reaching into the template (modal-shell R5, #420).
Only Notifications docks its dialog to the window edge (modal-shell R17, owner-approved #638); every other modal keeps the centred shell.

patterns.title: Leaderboard row
patterns.summary: Leaderboard sections share one fitted column plan, a 48-unit minimum row (percentile rows included) whose loading skeleton matches loaded rows at every text size, contained marquee names with motion-safe fallback, aligned pinned rows and one in-content pager per platform (never toolbar or rail items, on the Duo screen beside the vertical bar when unfolded, #345, #361), the selected row pinned above the pager on every page of full boards, one selected-row rule (jump off-page, open the profile on-page) for players and bands, whose own row inside a board or preview speaks its rank as "Your rank, <ordinal>" (bands "Your band, …") so the highlight is never the only cue (#457), a pinned row that follows the rows instead when at accessibility text sizes it would cover more than a third of the board (#386), with the owner-approved #370 variant that a Compete preview's separate rank row jumps to the full board at the player's position (Apple and Android Compete cards; Windows overview instrument cards, as they draw Compete), the owner-approved #364 variant that a song board in a split's trailing pane turns every row and its pinned row into a multi-row card (full name above rank and score, chevron centred) when any name would marquee, and one measured section-wide score-footer stack plan that never truncates the score, keyboard or screen-reader focus that scrolls a row clear of the floating pinned row and pager (WCAG 2.4.11, #409), and the owner-approved #543 variant that native song boards, Full Rankings, Band Rankings and Song Detail band previews draw a page's rows in one card with separators (the web keeps a card per row), extended on Windows by #643 to Song Detail's instrument and band previews, the Leaderboards overview boards and their First Run demos (in-card GroupedRows slices, View All inside the card), and rank-history rows (Leaderboards, Profile, Band) that draw rank and value in fixed right-aligned tabular columns measured once over every chart day, so the bold newest row and the tapped bar's detail line up, the date moves above the columns at large text and, when even the columns don't fit side by side, each keeps its measured width right-aligned on its own line, in rows at least 48 units tall (#594).

guards.message: Board pagination stays in the content under the board as RankingsPagerView, never as toolbar or rail items (leaderboard-row R5, #345).
Pinned selected-row footers use pinnedFooterControl(identifier:) for the row button style (Mac focus ring, Return, hover), not their own button style (leaderboard-row R7, #461).
Leaderboard marquee behavior has one shared owner (leaderboard-row R3).
The trailing-pane multi-row card decision has one owner (leaderboard-row R3 variant, #364): use songLeaderboardSectionColumns, not a second name fit.
The leaderboard row baseline is defined once (leaderboard-row R2).
The leaderboard row baseline is defined once (leaderboard-row R2).
Board pagination belongs to the shared pager (leaderboard-row R5).
Score footers share one section-wide stack plan; extend BandScoreFooterPanel/BandScoreFooterSection instead (leaderboard-row R8).

patterns.title: Load transition
patterns.summary: Initial loads use one gate, and page tools and notices acting on the gated content appear with it (the Paths Karaoke notice waits until every path form on screen has loaded, #649); selector and page reloads use a latest-wins content-to-spinner-to-content swap; stale content never shows under the spinner, and a pinned score row is stale only when its key (instrument, metric, leeway) changes, staying in place through page-only reloads like the web footer; a board pager appears only once a loaded page count above one is known (never a placeholder 1 / 1, #575) and keeps the last count while only the page reloads (Windows also hides it from an in-place board switch until the new count loads, #575 decision); graph card lists run the web out/height/in list sequence, chart swaps keep the card's size and paging a chart slides it to the new window over the web 400 ms (#593 decision); the spinner is one named busy indicator that reads after any retained header; a scroll during the first-load stagger fades the rest in together (web stagger rush) and never replays an entrance; selected-row reveals wait for the row's entrance; reduced motion removes fades; accordion-style reveals (owner-approved #561 variant) grow the height then fade the content in, and fade it out then collapse; a native card that groups several rows (the board group cards) fades in as one unit with all its rows, never staggering them inside it (owner-approved #614 variant); a new publication refreshes open pages in place without pausing their rows (R9; Android one announced Songs spinner and in-place re-reads elsewhere, #616).

guards.message: Reloadable result areas must remain in the shared load-transition inventory (load-transition R1).

Pages install the shared entrance window with festivalFadeInScope(resetKey:) or festivalScrollFadeInScope(_:resetKey:); a page that builds its own FestivalFadeInScope must be listed so its scroll rush and selected-row reveal stay on the shared rules (load-transition R5).

Lists get their entrance window from FadeIn.Stagger/Restagger; a page that builds its own StaggerArm must be listed so its scroll rush, replay guard and selected-row reveal stay on the shared rules (load-transition R5, #323).
Pages inside PublicationRefreshBoundary set their title with festivalNavigationTitle so the VoiceOver page anchor can name them during a publication refresh (load-transition R9).
@AccessibilityFocusState invalidates the view that owns it while lists scroll; keep it on a small leaf view or modifier, never on a view that builds a page's content (load-transition R9, #325).
Reloadable result areas must remain in the shared load-transition inventory (load-transition R1).
Reloadable result areas must remain in the shared load-transition inventory (load-transition R1).
Graph card lists must remain in the shared load-transition inventory (load-transition R7).

Accordion-style reveals go through the shared AccordionReveal / AccordionRevealOf (height, then fade in; fade out, then collapse; instant under reduced motion), never a local expand/shrink transition (load-transition R10, #561).

Every Expander gets the shared accordion motion from the implicit Expander style (Accordion.Sequenced); a custom disclosure panel that drives its own AccordionMover must be listed so its grow-then-fade timing stays shared (load-transition R10, #561).

patterns.title: Accordion
patterns.summary: Every in-place expand/collapse (filter-sheet disclosure groups, switch-revealed blocks, selector panels, Settings choice rows) opens the container first and then fades its content in, and fades the content out before collapsing (150 ms each, web QUICK_FADE_MS; owner #561). Steps are interruptible, Reduce Motion keeps only the fade, VoiceOver hears the requested state at once and transparent content is hidden and takes no touches. One shared component per platform.

guards.message: Accordions share one motion: use FestivalDisclosureGroup (or FestivalAccordionState + festivalAccordion(_:follows:) + FestivalAccordionContent for a reveal) instead of a raw DisclosureGroup (accordion R1, R5).

patterns.title: Empty and error states
patterns.summary: Loading, empty, paused/unavailable and failed outcomes stay distinct: every empty page or region uses the shared centred title/subtitle empty state with no card and no Reset Filters or Retry button (only a prerequisite action such as Choose Profile, whose prominent fill and label stay paired and legible under Increase Contrast, #477); syncing, publication-paused and unavailable states use the shared unavailable status with Retry; one loading indicator, a white arc on a 10% white track at the web Spinner sizes (web ArcSpinner; Apple FestivalArcProgressStyle, #635), exposed as a single named busy indicator; explicit unavailable messages without global-search Retry controls; a score-update scrape freeze 503 for a URL the shared pinned-read client already verified in the same, still-current publication returns that kept body instead of the service status (R9, #554); cold reads, outages, non-score freezes and other publications still fail with Retry. Kept bodies are in-memory: Android uses a byte-bounded LRU; Apple's verified JSON entries are cleared on every publication change but currently have no byte budget (R9 Known debt). An inline service status is one container whose message, countdown and Retry stay separately reachable; Retry keeps its own identifier and an iOS 44×44 pt target, and a consumer tagging the wrapper contains its children first (R10, #463).

guards.message: Global Search reruns from submit or edit; it has no Retry control (empty-error-states R3).
Empty states have no Reset/Clear Filters button; filters reset from their flyout or sheet (empty-error-states R8).
Use the shared FestivalEmptyState (empty-error-states R5/R8); ContentUnavailableView failed Dynamic Type audits.

Indeterminate spinners are FestivalLoadingView (the arc on a faint track, one named busy indicator; empty-error-states R5/R6, #635), never a raw ProgressView. Determinate ProgressView(value:) bars are exempt.
Empty states are centred text with no card or Reset button (empty-error-states R8, #377).
Syncing, paused and unavailable states are not no-results: use ServiceUnavailableView with Retry, not FestivalEmptyState (empty-error-states R1/R8).
Empty states have no Reset Filters button; the filter sheet's Reset is the way back (empty-error-states R8, #377).

An empty state in a list or grid fills the region its controls and pager leave (rememberEmptyRegion + fillEmptyRegion), never a fixed-height block (empty-error-states R2, #377). Only the content-sized Notifications sheet keeps a minimum.

patterns.title: Quick Links
patterns.summary: One native Quick Links controller per page preserves web section order, uses a 32-unit shared landing/current line, and exposes an accessible current section through the platform chooser; a nested section can be a card inside its parent row, landing at its measured offset (Profile Rank History and Percentiles, #590).

guards.message: Apple Quick Links menus are constructed only by the shared toolbar component (quick-links R1, R2).
Android Quick Links controllers belong to the shared Compose implementation (quick-links R1).
Windows Quick Links menu UI belongs to QuickLinksMenuButton (quick-links R1, R5).

patterns.title: Chart date axis
patterns.summary: History bar charts centre each date label on its own bar on every page and text size, keep labels horizontal rather than the web's angled ticks (agent decision #314), pin end labels inside the chart instead of clipping, hide colliding labels (newest kept), label only visible bars and keep tick text out of the accessibility tree.

guards.message: Apple chart date axes come from the shared barChartDateAxis, which centres each date on its bar (chart-date-axis R1, R4).
Bar-chart date labels are placed by ChartGeometry.bandLabelLefts, not per-chart centring math (chart-date-axis R1, R4-R6).
Bar-chart dates are laid out by the ChartBandLabels row, whose height follows the text size; canvases don't draw dates in a fixed band (chart-date-axis R4, R5).

patterns.title: Song leaderboard header
patterns.summary: A song-scoped leaderboard (instrument or band size) names the song first in an in-page header with the board on the line under the artist, keeps that header on screen through board, page and player reloads (only the rows reload), keeps the bar title empty until the header scrolls away, and sits on the song's static dimmed album art. Owner-approved variant (#342): a board opened beside Song Detail in a split's trailing pane drops the song header and is titled by its instrument icon and name (or band size). Android adopts the variant with its on-demand split (#583).

guards.message: Song leaderboards sit on the song's static album art, festivalBackground(.song) (song-leaderboard-header R4).
Song leaderboard bar titles come from the shared SongBarTitleToolbarItem, or InstrumentPageTitleToolbarItem beside Song Detail (song-leaderboard-header R3, R5, Variants #342; song-header R4).
Song pages show their static cover through SongCoverBackdrop, each page for itself (song-leaderboard-header R4).
Song leaderboards name the song first; the board is the header's board line, never a '{Board} Leaderboard' title (song-leaderboard-header R1).
Windows song leaderboards take their title from Controls/SongLeaderboardHeader (song-leaderboard-header R5).

patterns.title: Song header
patterns.summary: Song pages show the song through one shared header whose title and artist each fill the width beside the art on one line and marquee only on overflow (Reduce Motion truncates, accessibility sizes wrap in-page); one compact pinned bar title marquees on one line and appears only once the header scrolls away, under the iPhone Duo vertical bar too (owner-approved, #363).

guards.message: Song headers show the title with the shared SongHeaderText / SongBarTitle (one full-width marqueeing line), not a page-local Text (song-header R1, R5).

Song header titles use the shared SongHeaderText column (one MarqueeText line that scrolls on overflow and wraps in-page at 150%+ text), never a page-local TextBlock or MarqueeText (song-header R1, R2, R3).
Only the song pages keep their navigation bar from minimizing, through songBarTitleKeepsBarVisible (song-header R4 Duo variant, page-tools-and-nav-chrome R14 exception, #363).

patterns.title: View all call to action
patterns.summary: A card of preview rows ends with one full-width brand-purple button after the rows (on Apple inside the group card as FestivalGlassSection's action, a flat opaque purple and never Liquid Glass, agent decision #382; on Android inside the GlassCard of Song Detail's instrument, band and Score History cards, #588; on the Windows, Android and Apple profile each Duos/Trios/Quads group is one card ending in it, owner-approved variant #596) (View Full Leaderboard, View All Rivals, View All on Rival Detail categories, View All Rankings (N), View All Scores) at the platform minimum target, with no per-consumer overrides, a label-first accessible name and readable contrast-mode colours. The preview keeps its capped length: the button navigates to the full list's own page (pushed, or the trailing pane in a split; Song Detail View All Scores opens Player History with its sorts) and never expands the card in place (R8, owner #324); Leaderboards' View All Rankings opens Full Rankings beside the overview (#352).

guards.message: Windows View all labels come from ViewAllCta so every CTA keeps the web copy and the label-first name rule (view-all-cta R4).
Bind a View all CTA's text and name to its view model (ViewAllText/ViewAllName via ViewAllCta) and use FSTViewAllButtonStyle (view-all-cta R3, R4).
Windows has one View all CTA style, FSTViewAllButtonStyle in Themes/Styles.xaml; extend it instead of adding another (view-all-cta R3).

patterns.title: Stat tile grid
patterns.summary: Profile and Band stat tile grids: a tile whose value or label would wrap in one slot spans two (owner-approved variant #591, Android), tiles keep web order with the row's last tile widening instead of holes, every tile takes the grid's tallest height, and text that doesn't fit two slots wraps rather than truncating. A centred tile with a trailing chevron pads both sides by the chevron's clearance so its text is centred on the card (#651). One grid component per platform.

guards.message: Stat tile grids place and size tiles in one place: use StatTileGrid (spans, web order, one height) instead of chunked rows with intrinsic heights (stat-tile-grid R1-R5).

patterns.title: Settings value row
patterns.summary: A read-only Settings title/value row (Version rows, Service Info state) keeps the value beside the title only when the title's natural width, a 12-unit gap and the value fit; otherwise the value stacks 4 units under the title and supporting text. It is one non-interactive accessibility item, and each platform has one component for it.

guards.message: Settings title/value rows measure their fit in one place: use SettingsValueRow (supporting/trailing slots) instead of another intrinsic-width Layout (settings-value-row R1, R4).
Settings title/value rows decide inline vs stacked in one place: use SettingsValueRow (detail/value slots) instead of another text-size AnyLayout switch (settings-value-row R1, R4).
Settings title/value rows stack by measured fit in SettingValueGrid, never by Windows text size in code-behind (settings-value-row R1, R4; #539).

patterns.title: Settings toggle row
patterns.summary: A Settings on/off row (title, description, disabled reason, trailing switch) is one switch element whose whole row is the touch target: at least 44 pt on iOS/iPadOS and 56 dp on Android, one flip per tap, no flip while disabled, applied once per platform so new switches inherit it. The Mac keeps the system switch at its control size.

guards.message: Settings switches get their whole-row target from settingsRowToggles() at the page root; a per-switch toggleStyle would replace it (settings-toggle-row R1, R6).

patterns.title: Back keeps place
patterns.summary: Back to a cached or back-stack page keeps its loaded content (keyed reload gate; new publication or account reloads, failures retry), rebuilds and replays nothing, moves nothing (Windows pauses focus-follow scrolling and scroll anchoring while away) and, on Windows, returns focus to the opener in its original focus state. In an Apple on-demand split, Back on the leading page closes the open trailing pane first and keeps the page; a second Back leaves it. A player or band profile is a full page that covers the split, and its Back returns to the kept split (#352). Android (#583) follows the same order: system Back pops the pane's stack, then closes the pane, then leaves the page.

guards.message: Cached pages pause focus-follow scrolling and scroll anchoring only through CachedPageScroll, which restores them on return (back-keeps-place R3); extend it instead of pausing scrollers page by page.

patterns.title: Songs profile panel
patterns.summary: On wide Songs rows (iPad, iPhone Duo inner display, Mac) with a selected player or band whose score index is available and publication-matched, the row splits: song on the left, that profile's compact score cards (per scored instrument, or one band card) on the right. Compact cards keep one line or the row stays plain; loading, paused, failed, accessibility sizes and Shop rows keep today's row; with Filter Invalid Scores on the cards show effective scores (invalid-scores, #613). Card fields follow the saved Song Row Visual Order only while Independent Visual Order is on, else the web default order (MetadataField.songRowOrder).

patterns.title: Invalid scores (Filter Invalid Scores)
patterns.summary: With Settings > Filter Invalid Scores on and a player selected, each chart shows its effective score like the web's effectiveScores: the raw score when valid at the leeway (ml, else the CHOpt ceiling), else the first validScores variant valid at the leeway (rank from rankTiers, population from populationTiers), else the legacy validScore, else none; Over CHOpt Threshold keeps the raw score. Rows, chips, metadata, the profile panel, filters and sorts use effective scores and nothing pauses. Songs rows flag replaced/dropped scores with the red (gold for over-threshold) indicator, its own 44 pt accessible button after the song, opening the Filtered Score alert (OK / Settings). Song Details uses the web's filterPlayerScores rule. Player Profile and Statistics aggregate the effective scores (R4) of any viewed player, selected or not, and re-aggregate in place when the setting or leeway changes; only the Over CHOpt Threshold count stays raw (R9, web PlayerContent, #619).

guards.regex: not available yet|paused while Filter Invalid Scores
guards.message: Filter Invalid Scores substitutes effective scores (invalid-scores R3, #613); never pause rows, panels, filters or sorts. Use InvalidScorePolicy.

patterns.title: Hinge columns
patterns.summary: While a vertical fold crosses a layout (iPhone Duo book pose, Android book posture), grid and two-up row gutters sit on the fold with the same column count each side, full-width titles wrap on their own side, and the flat layout returns in place when unfolded; fully unfolded (flat), splits and page rows divide at the midpoint of the free content area, never on the flat hinge line (owner-approved, #361); cells sharing a row start at its top edge (#365) and a card of several elements is one accessibility container read whole (#490; Android card grids are row-major LazyVerticalGrids and Band Detail pairs its sections in top-aligned rows under a full-width header, never masonry lanes, #584); two-pane viewers (Paths Side by Side) use HingePanes, meeting at the fold in book pose and as equal halves when flat (owner-approved, #368).

guards.message: Page grids use HingeGrid so their gutter sits on an iPhone Duo fold in book pose (hinge-columns R1, R6); the First Run Shop demo is a fixed miniature inside a slide.

Card grids are row-major (LazyVerticalGrid through AdaptiveCardGrid, ProfileGrid or the Suggestions grid) so sections side by side start on their row's top edge however far the page scrolls; masonry lanes drift apart (hinge-columns R8, #584).

patterns.title: Wide columns
patterns.summary: Page rows and cards show in two columns only in wide landscape windows (iPad landscape, iPhone Duo unfolded landscape, a wide Mac surface), row-major under full-width headings (pages of unequal section cards such as the Mac Settings window panes flow column by column in balanced columns; the Settings page on iPad, iPhone Duo and Android tablets/foldables is a list/detail split instead, split-panes R6, owner-approved #371), meeting at the Duo hinge in book pose and at the free content area's midpoint when fully unfolded (owner-approved, #361), reflowing without reloading; portrait, compact windows and (for Settings) accessibility text sizes keep one column; the Item Shop list pairs its rows (its card grid keeps its own even-column policy); full-width leaderboards pair rank rows row-major under one full-width pinned row and pager, while split sub-pages stay one column. Owner-approved Android variant (#581): Android Songs shows two row-major columns in any landscape window or across a vertical fold with room for two 320 dp columns (no height-class gate), one column in portrait, at large text or under TalkBack, and no longer splits list/detail (a tap pushes Song Detail).

patterns.title: Split panes
patterns.summary: The boundary between a list/detail split's panes draws no divider line: the band (a fold only when partially folded, owner-approved #361; otherwise a 1 pt band at the free content area's midpoint plus each pane's full-page margins) separates them, a midpoint draws a 1 pt hairline only under the system's or the app's Increase Contrast (the band is never an accessibility element), and the split's one backdrop and top gradient run unbroken across the band. Owner-approved variant R6 (#371; iPad, iPhone Duo inner landscape and Android tablets/foldables): Settings always splits, showing a vertically centred placeholder (Settings icon, "Settings", "Select a setting to see more options here") until a chevron row opens its options on the right; plain toggles act in the list. Owner-approved Android variant R7 (#583): Android tablets, foldables and wide windows use the iPhone Duo's on-demand split: Rivals/All Rivals/Compete open Rival Detail, Leaderboards opens Full/Band Rankings and Song Detail opens its boards and Score History in a trailing pane when the window is landscape, regular and leaves 360 dp a pane, or at the fold in book posture; everything else stays one page, and Back closes the pane first.

guards.message: Split panes are separated by space, not a drawn divider; a hairline only under high contrast at a midpoint (split-panes R1, R2).

patterns.title: Catalogue sort
patterns.summary: Pages that list catalogue songs (Songs, Item Shop) sort through the platform's Songs Sort sheet/flyout: one radio group of the page's modes, the shared Sort Direction section, Reset to Title ascending, a gold trigger with a '<Mode>, <direction>' state, per-page saved choice, one comparator (web useFilteredSongs) for grid, list and hinge layouts, and a visible pause when a mode's data is missing. Item Shop offers Title, Artist, Year and Duration on native and web (agent decision #379).

guards.message: Catalogue Sort sheets (Songs, Item Shop, first-run demo) reuse SongsSheets SortDirectionSection; never copy the Sort Direction rows (catalogue-sort R1). Score History's segmented Sort Scores row is a separate control.
Windows catalogue Sort flyouts (Songs, Item Shop) host Controls/SongSortForm with their own Draft, Title and IdPrefix; never copy its Sort By / Direction groups into a page (catalogue-sort R1).

patterns.title: Experimental ranks
patterns.summary: Settings → Enable Experimental Leaderboard Ranks (off by default, reset by Reset) is the one gate for the experimental ranking metrics app-wide like the web: while off, Rank By offers Total Score only and is hidden in-page (the Mac View › Rank By submenu lists only Total Score); saved, routed and selected metrics are coerced to Total Score at read time, never rewritten; turning it off returns open pages to Total Score; on offers Adjusted, Weighted, FC Rate and Max Score (bands without Max Score); Rivals Rank By, profile rank tiles, rank notifications (web projection) and the first-run slide follow it (#541).

guards.message: Rank By menus and metric lists offer RankingMetric.enabled / BandRankingMetric.enabled (or a view model's gated options), never every metric, so Settings → Experimental Ranks gates them (experimental-ranks R1).

Rank By choices come from the experimental-ranks gate (RankingMetric.enabled(experimentalRanks:), BandRankingMetric.enabled, RivalRankMetric.enabled); never list allCases in UI (experimental-ranks R1).

Rank By menus offer RankingMetricInfo.Enabled / BandRankingMetricInfo.Enabled (a view model's gated MetricOptions), never every metric, so Settings → Experimental Ranks gates them (experimental-ranks R1). Band Detail and the Rivals hub list every metric only behind ShowRankBy / ShowMetricPicker.

patterns.title: Instrument chip rows
patterns.summary: Songs row instrument status chips that don't fit one line wrap onto the fewest balanced lines (9 → 5 + 4, earlier lines take the extra chip), each centred across the card under the art and title, measured from the chip area's own width, in service order with one spoken row name. Chips never clip, overlap or shrink; natives drop the web's three-row cap, four-chip rule and hysteresis (agent decision #645).

patterns.title: Item Shop offer status
patterns.summary: New and Leaving Tomorrow on Songs rows, Item Shop list rows, Item Shop grid cards and first-run demo rows: New is the gold outline alone with no chip, pill or sparkles glyph (operator 2026-09-28 for Songs; #562 for the Shop), only Leaving Tomorrow gets a visible indicator (red clock circle or pill, before the bag and chevron), and both states stay in the row or card's accessible name. Highlighting off or a hidden Shop shows no state. The outline and pill follow a live contrast switch (#516).

guards.message: Item Shop New is the gold outline alone; no sparkles glyph or New pill (shop-offer-status R1, #562). Use ShopNewStatusMarker for the spoken state.
Songs/Shop rows draw no New glyph (shop-offer-status R1); only ShopLeavingIndicator is visible (R2).
Android Item Shop New has no visible badge or sparkle (shop-offer-status R1, #562); TalkBack hears it through stateDescription (R3).

patterns.title: Rival rows
patterns.summary: Rows inside Rivals cards: the hub's rival rows and the song comparison rows on Rival Detail, Rivalry and the Duo category cards. One row component per kind on every surface, one shared red/green status capsule with text (readable red text), album art leading every song row through the shared ArtworkTile (art vertically centred alone, above the instrument icon when both, owner #558), one spoken element per row that names who leads, and pills that stack and wrap at accessibility sizes. Apple, Android and Windows song rows show '#rank Name' pills for both sides, the leader green and the trailer red, with a rank-delta badge and no scores (agent decisions #558, #603, owner may override). Each rival list is one card of rows with hairlines, never a card per row (R6, owner #603): the hub and Compete rivals cards with View All inside, each Rival Detail category, and All Rivals and Rivalry (Android lazy card segments, Windows grouped ListView slices).

patterns.title: Band member lines
patterns.summary: A band card lists one line per member with the name leading on one shared edge (row to row and card to card) and the member's value (song score) and instrument icons trailing; the whole card stacks each member's icons under its name when any member can't fit inline (name clamped 96-180 plus gaps) or at large text, long names marquee/truncate/wrap inside their column, and the member lines stay inside the card's one screen-reader stop (#589).

patterns.title: Search scopes: global and profile search
patterns.summary: Every song/player/band search runs the platform's global-search engine with the kinds it needs as targets; the profile search offers All · Players · Bands and starts on All with players and bands searched together (owner #600, web SearchModal targets players|bands), names the scope's targets in its prompt ("Search players or bands"), reuses global search's rows, order and All-only titles, opens a player or a band's page (no gate message), and uses a native scope control with an explicit All (Apple scope bar, Android M3 segmented buttons, Windows SelectorBar; agent decision #600). Find Rival stays players-only.

patterns.title: Metadata pills
patterns.summary: The season chip (S15) and percentile chip (Top N%) are one shared component each per platform, one size everywhere (chip label style, 24 dp tall, 8 dp corners, season >= 48 dp, percentile >= 5.5 em), with the web colours: seasons textSecondary on surfaceSubtle with a borderSubtle outline and the catalogue's current season inverted; Top 1% skewed gold outline, Top 5% gold outline, else 10% white. Season pills read 'Season N' / 'Current season N' (#606). In a metadata row every chip beside them (accuracy/FC, difficulty, stars, intensity) reads at the same visible pill height, and a full-combo accuracy is the percent alone in the Top 1% skewed gold outline (web AccuracyDisplay fcBadge, #644).

guards.message: Season and percentile chips use the shared ui/design/MetadataPills.kt components (metadata-pills R1).
Season and percentile chips come from Controls/MetadataPills.cs, whose roles live in Festival.Core MetadataPillStyle (metadata-pills R1).
